title: While the list is scrolling it takes no hover and no clicks; the freeze lifts 150 ms after the last movement
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Sidebar/SidebarView.swift:136-147 - `.onScrollPhaseChange { _, phase in if phase == .idle { scrollSettle?.cancel(); isListScrolling = false } else { noteListScroll() } }` and `.onScrollGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self, of: { $0.contentOffset.y }) { old, new in if old != new { noteListScroll() } }`

DroppyCode/App/Views/Sidebar/SidebarView.swift:391-403 noteListScroll - `if !isListScrolling { isListScrolling = true }`, cancels and restarts a task that sleeps `.milliseconds(150)` then clears the flag if not cancelled and still set
preconditions: Sidebar list has enough content to scroll.
action: User scrolls the list with a wheel, trackpad or drag.
expected_result: Hit testing is disabled for the whole list for as long as scrolling continues and for 150 ms after the last movement. Wheel ticks report no scroll phase, so they keep the freeze alive through the contentOffset observer alone. A scroll phase reaching `.idle` cancels the settle task and lifts the freeze immediately rather than waiting the 150 ms. The flag is written only when it is currently false, so a continuous scroll costs one list evaluation, not one per frame.
side_effects: Starts and cancels a debounce task on the main actor.
failure_cases: Task cancelled by a newer scroll: the older task returns without clearing the flag.
cancellation: The settle task is cancelled by every subsequent movement and by an idle phase.
windows_path: A 150 ms debounce timer on the Windows list plus pointer-events suppression while it is armed. The idle-phase shortcut needs a Windows scroll-end signal (WM_MOUSEWHEEL has none; a scrollbar release or inertia-end from the input stack supplies it, and without one the 150 ms debounce alone governs). Platform boundary: scroll phase reporting.
verification_method: interaction test that a click landing during a scroll is ignored and lands 150 ms later.

title: threads(in:) orders a project's top-level threads: open before settled, settled by latest settled first, pinned before unpinned, then sortOrder ascending with unplaced threads on top, then newest created first
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/AppModel.swift:314-333 threads(in:) - filters `!isArchived && !isInPanel`, drops any thread whose parent is among them, then sorts: `if lhs.isSettled != rhs.isSettled { return rhs.isSettled }`; `if lhs.isSettled { return Self.settledFirst(lhs, rhs) }`; `if lhs.isPinned != rhs.isPinned { return lhs.isPinned }`; then `(lhs.sortOrder, rhs.sortOrder)` with `(left?, right?) where left != right` giving `left < right`, `(nil, .some)` giving true, `(.some, nil)` giving false, default `lhs.createdAt > rhs.createdAt`
DroppyCode/App/AppModel.swift:377-380 - `nonisolated static func settledFirst(_ lhs: ChatThread, _ rhs: ChatThread) -> Bool { (lhs.settledAt ?? lhs.updatedAt) > (rhs.settledAt ?? rhs.updatedAt) }`
preconditions: A project with threads.
action: The project layout asks for the project's threads.
expected_result: Archived threads and threads currently shown in a floating panel are excluded. A thread whose parent is also in the shown set is excluded (it appears as a helper under its parent instead); a thread whose parent is gone or archived is included as a top-level row. The comparator is exactly as quoted, including the rule that a thread with no sortOrder sorts before one that has it, and that settled threads fall back to updatedAt when settledAt is nil.
persistence: Reads thread.sortOrder, thread.settledAt, thread.isPinned, thread.isSettled, thread.createdAt, thread.isArchived, thread.isInPanel, thread.parentThreadID.
windows_path: The comparator must be implemented as a total order with the same tie-breaks; the `(nil, .some)` asymmetry is deliberate and is not a stable-sort accident.
